newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa stocks end near lows as Wall St slips.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa stocks end near lows as Wall St slips.

text.p: South African shares closed near their day lows on Thursday as a weaker Wall Street led global markets away from their recent record highs, dealers said.
Wall Street stocks, after dipping on Wednesday, opened weaker after new jobless claims data triggered renewed concern about tightness in the U.S. labour market.
"A weaker Wall Street and (London's) FTSE-100 took us down with them. Most sectors here seem to have ended down," one dealer said.

The all-share index fell 27.6 points to 7,031.5 as industrials dipped 28.7 points to 8,238.7. Earlier in the week some dealers had expected the Johannesburg Stock Exchange overall index to breach its life high of 7,086.8 if Wall Street managed to hold gains above 6,000.
However, dealers said the outlook for the U.S. market was still positive and no serious correction was seen. South African markets would continue to track the Dow on Friday, they added.

The gold index ended down only 2.8 points to 1,740.0 after finding support from better bullion, silver and platinum prices. But the overall downward market trend had made positive gains in golds impossible to secure.
"The bullion price was up, but gold shares did not manage to respond positively," one dealer said.
